Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# tailspin — A log file highlighter

tailspin highlights log files for easier reading. It can read from files or from stdin and supports printing
highlighted output to stdout or viewing interactively with a pager.

Usage examples:

- Read a file and view with the pager:
  tspin application.log

- Pipe into tspin and print to stdout:
  echo "hello" | tspin

- Follow a file (tail -f like behavior):
  tspin -f application.log

Installation:

- Homebrew: brew install tailspin
- Cargo: cargo install tailspin
- Package managers: check your platform's package repository

For more information, see the man page in the man/ directory (if present) and the example logs in example-logs/.

.SH "NAME"
tspin \- A log file highlighter
.SH "SYNOPSIS"
.sp
\fBtspin\fP [\fIOPTION\fP]... [\fIFILE\fP]...
.SH "DESCRIPTION"
.sp
tailspin is a command line tool that highlights log files.
.SH "OPTIONS"
.sp
\fI\-f, \-\-follow\fP
.RS 4
Follow (tail) the contents of the file.
Always true when using the \fI\-\-follow\-command\fP flag.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-p, \-\-print\fP
.RS 4
Print the output to stdout instead of viewing the contents in the pager \fIless\fP.
Always true if using stdin.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-config\-path\fP \fBCONFIG_PATH\fP
.RS 4
Specify the path to a custom configuration file.
Defaults to \fBXDG_CONFIG_HOME/tailspin/theme.toml\fP or \fB~/.config/tailspin/theme.toml\fP if not set.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-e, \-\-exec\fP \fBCOMMAND\fP
.RS 4
Run command and view the output in a pager.
The command traps the interrupt signal to allow for cancelling and resuming follow mode while inside \fIless\fP.
.sp
.B Example:
.br
.sp
.if n .RS 4
.nf
.fam C
tspin \-\-listen\-command \*(Aqkubectl logs \-f pod_name\*(Aq
.fam
.fi
.if n .RE
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-highlight\fP \fBCOLOR1\fP:\fIword1,word2,...\fP \fBCOLOR2\fP:\fIword3,word4,...\fP
.RS 4
Highlight the provided comma\-separated words in the specified color.
Possible colors are red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, and cyan.
.sp
.B Example:
.br
.sp
.if n .RS 4
.nf
.fam C
tspin logfile.txt \-\-highlight red:error,fail \-\-highlight green:success,ok
.fam
.fi
.if n .RE
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-enable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP
.RS 4
Disable all highlighting groups except the ones specified.
Comma separated list of groups.
Cannot be used with \fB\-\-disable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-disable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP
.RS 4
Disable the specified highlighting groups.
Comma separated list of groups.
Cannot be used with \fB\-\-enable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-disable\-builtin\-keywords\fP
.RS 4
Disables the highlighting of all builtin keyword groups (booleans, severity and REST).
.RE
.SH "ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES"
.sp
\fBTAILSPIN_PAGER\fP
.RS 4
Set the \fITAILSPIN_PAGER\fP environment variable to override the default pager.
The command must include the string \fI[FILE]\fP which will be replaced with the file path internally.
For example, \fI"ov \-f [FILE]"\fP.
.RE

.sp
\fBless\fP(1), \fBtail\fP(1)

Ben Sadeh (github.com/bensadeh/tailspin)

import subprocess, os
def run(args, inp=None, env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env=e)
    return p

# pager tests - need to understand default pager is less
# When file is given without -p and stdout is not tty (piped), what happens?
# Our tests use capture_output (pipe), so pager would be invoked? But earlier -p tests worked.
# Let's see what happens without -p when stdout is pipe
open("/tmp/a.log","w").write("ERROR hello\n")
p=run(["/tmp/a.log"])
print("no -p with pipe stdout:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# with stdin pipe but no file, no -p? Earlier stdin gave print. Let's test stdin with -p vs without
p=run([], inp="ERROR hi\n")
print("stdin no args:", repr(p.stdout))
p=run(["-p"], inp="ERROR hi\n")
print("stdin -p:", repr(p.stdout))
p=run(["-f"], inp="ERROR hi\n")
print("stdin -f:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:200]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# --pager
p=run(["--pager","cat [FILE]","/tmp/a.log"])
print("pager cat:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# TAILSPIN_PAGER env
p=run(["/tmp/a.log"], env={"TAILSPIN_PAGER":"cat [FILE]"})
print("env pager:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# --pager without [FILE]?
p=run(["--pager","cat","/tmp/a.log"])
print("pager without [FILE]:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:1000]))

# --exec
p=run(["--exec","echo hello"])
print("exec echo:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# --exec with pager override?

p=run(["-p","--exec","echo hello"])
print("exec with -p:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# --follow with -p on file?
# Need to test follow behavior with timeout - follow should block. Use timeout 2s
import threading
def test_follow():
    import subprocess
    p=subprocess.Popen(["./executable","-f","-p","/tmp/a.log"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    try:
        out,err=p.communicate(timeout=2)
        print("follow -p output:", repr(out[:500]), "err:", repr(err[:500]), "rc:", p.returncode)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        p.kill()
        out,err=p.communicate()
        print("follow timed out (expected, it blocks) out:", repr(out[:500] if out else ""))
        # check if it printed initial content?
test_follow()

import subprocess
def run(args, inp=""):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

# more highlight edge
for a in [["--highlight","red:foo,"],["--highlight","red:,foo"],["--highlight","red:foo,,bar"],["--highlight","red:"],["--highlight","red:foo:bar"]]:
    # test with matching input to see what words actually highlight
    for line in ["foo", "bar", "", "foo:bar", ":", ","]:
        rc,out,err=run(a, line+"\n")
        # need to disable others to isolate?
        # use full with disable all + builtin disabled to see custom only
        p2=subprocess.run(["./executable","--disable-builtin-keywords","--disable","numbers,urls,pointers,dates,paths,quotes,key-value-pairs,uuids,ip-addresses,processes,json"]+a, input=line+"\n", capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        print(f"args={a} line={line!r} full={repr(out)} isolated={repr(p2.stdout)}")

print("=== enable/disable edge ===")
for a in [["--enable","numbers,numbers"], ["--disable","numbers,numbers"], ["--enable","numbers,urls,numbers"]]:
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+a, input="123 https://example.com\n", capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
    print(f"{a} -> {repr(p.stdout)}")

# test --highlight with spaces?
for hw in ["red:foo bar", "red: foo", " red:foo"]:
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable","--highlight",hw], input="test\n", capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
    print(f"highlight {hw!r} -> rc={p.returncode} err={repr(p.stderr[:300])}")

# test combined short flags: -fp, -pf, -fe etc?

# test --follow without file with stdin?

for a in [["--","--unknown"], ["--","/tmp/a.log"]]:

    print(f"{a} -> rc={p.returncode} out={repr(p.stdout[:200])} err={repr(p.stderr[:500])}")

# tailspin — A log file highlighter

tailspin highlights log files for easier reading. It can read from files or from stdin and supports printing
highlighted output to stdout or viewing interactively with a pager.

Usage examples:

- Read a file and view with the pager:
  tspin application.log

- Pipe into tspin and print to stdout:
  echo "hello" | tspin

- Follow a file (tail -f like behavior):
  tspin -f application.log

Installation:

- Homebrew: brew install tailspin
- Cargo: cargo install tailspin
- Package managers: check your platform's package repository

For more information, see the man page in the man/ directory (if present) and the example logs in example-logs/.

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, builder::PossibleValuesParser};

fn cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("tspin")
        .version("5.6.0")
        .about("A log file highlighter")
        .arg(Arg::new("FILE").help("Filepath"))
        .arg(Arg::new("follow").short('f').long("follow").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Follow the contents of a file"))
        .arg(Arg::new("print").short('p').long("print").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Print the output to stdout"))
        .arg(Arg::new("config-path").long("config-path").value_name("CONFIG_PATH").help("Provide a custom path to a configuration file"))
        .arg(Arg::new("exec").short('e').long("exec").value_name("EXEC").help("Run command and view the output in a pager"))
        .arg(Arg::new("highlight").long("highlight").value_name("COLOR_WORD").action(ArgAction::Append).help("Highlights in the form color:word1,word2"))
        .arg(Arg::new("enable").long("enable").value_name("ENABLED_HIGHLIGHTERS").action(ArgAction::Append).value_delimiter(',').value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new(["numbers","urls","pointers","dates","paths","quotes","key-value-pairs","uuids","ip-addresses","processes","json"])).help("Enable specific highlighters"))
        .arg(Arg::new("disable").long("disable").value_name("DISABLED_HIGHLIGHTERS").action(ArgAction::Append).value_delimiter(',').value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new(["numbers","urls","pointers","dates","paths","quotes","key-value-pairs","uuids","ip-addresses","processes","json"])).help("Disable specific highlighters"))
        .arg(Arg::new("disable-builtin-keywords").long("disable-builtin-keywords").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Disable the highlighting of all builtin keyword groups (booleans, nulls, log severities and common REST verbs)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("pager").long("pager").value_name("PAGER").help("Override the default pager command used by tspin. (e.g. `--pager=\"ov -f [FILE]\"`)"))
}

fn main() {
    let m = cli().try_get_matches();
    match m {
        Ok(_) => println!("ok"),
        Err(e) => e.exit(),
    }
}

pub fn load_theme(config_path_opt: Option<&str>) -> Result<Theme, AppError> {
    let mut theme = Theme::default_theme();
    fn dirs_fallback() -> Option<String> {
        if let Ok(home) = std::env::var("HOME") {
            Some(format!("{}/.config/tailspin/theme.toml", home))
        } else {
            None
        }
    }
    let path_str = match path_opt {
        Some(s) => s,
        None => return Ok(theme),
    };
    // check existence for default vs explicit?
    let is_explicit = config_path_opt.is_some();
    match std::fs::read_to_string(&path_str) {
        Ok(content) => {
            if content.trim().is_empty() {
                return Ok(theme);
            }
            match toml::from_str::<ThemeFile>(&content) {
                Ok(file) => {
                    theme.apply_file(file);
                    Ok(theme)
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    print_toml_error(&e);
                    Err(AppError{code:1})
                }
            }
        }
        Err(e) => {
            use std::io::ErrorKind;
            if e.kind() == ErrorKind::NotFound {
                if is_explicit {
                    eprintln!("Error:   × could not find the TOML file\n");
                    Err(AppError{code:1})
                } else {
                    Ok(theme)
                }
            } else {
                // other io error (e.g., IsADirectory)
                let msg = e.to_string();

                eprintln!("Error:   × could not read the TOML file: {}\n  ╰─▶ {}\n", msg, msg);
                Err(AppError{code:1})
            }
        }
    }
}

use crate::theme::{Theme, Style, Color};

struct Span { start: usize, end: usize, style: Style, is_keyword_bg: bool }

pub struct Highlighter {
    theme: Theme,
    enabled: HashSet<String>,
    disable_builtin: bool,
    custom: Vec<(Style, Vec<String>)>,
}
impl Highlighter {
    pub fn new(theme: &Theme, enable: &[String], disable: &[String], disable_builtin: bool, flag_highlights: Vec<(String, Vec<String>)>) -> Self {
        let all = ["numbers","urls","pointers","dates","paths","quotes","key-value-pairs","uuids","ip-addresses","processes","json"];
        let enabled: HashSet<String> = if !enable.is_empty() { enable.iter().cloned().collect() }
        else if !disable.is_empty() { let dis: HashSet<String> = disable.iter().cloned().collect(); all.iter().filter(|s| !dis.contains(&***s)).map(|s| s.to_string()).collect() }
        else { all.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect() };
        let mut custom: Vec<(Style, Vec<String>)> = Vec::new();
        for kw in &theme.custom_keywords {
            let words: Vec<String> = kw.words.iter().filter(|w| !w.is_empty()).cloned().collect();
            if words.is_empty() { continue; }
            custom.push((kw.style.clone(), words));
        }
        for (color_name, words) in flag_highlights {
            let style = color_to_style(&color_name);
            let filtered: Vec<String> = words.into_iter().filter(|w| !w.is_empty()).collect();
            if filtered.is_empty() { continue; }
            custom.push((style, filtered));
        }
        Self { theme: theme.clone(), enabled, disable_builtin, custom }
    }
    fn is_enabled(&self, name: &str) -> bool { self.enabled.contains(name) }
    pub fn highlight(&self, line: &str) -> String {
        let mut plain = line.to_string();
        let mut spans: Vec<Span> = Vec::new();
        // order: json, pointers, dates, ip, uuid, urls, paths, processes, kv, numbers, builtins, custom, quotes
        // Put pointers before dates to avoid shifting issues? Actually dates same length, pointers +1, so pointers before dates is better (as argued). Good.
        if self.is_enabled("json") { highlight_json_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("pointers") { highlight_pointers_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("dates") { highlight_dates_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("ip-addresses") { highlight_ip_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("uuids") { highlight_uuid_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("urls") { highlight_urls_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("paths") { highlight_paths_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("processes") { highlight_processes_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("key-value-pairs") { highlight_kv_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if self.is_enabled("numbers") { highlight_numbers_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        if !self.disable_builtin { highlight_builtins_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans); }
        highlight_custom_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.custom);
        if self.is_enabled("quotes") { highlight_quotes_plain(&mut plain, &mut spans, &self.theme); }
        // generate final ANSI
        generate_output(&plain, &spans)
    }
}
fn color_to_style(name: &str) -> Style {
    let c = match name.to_lowercase().as_str() {
        "red" => Color::Red, "green" => Color::Green, "yellow" => Color::Yellow,
        "blue" => Color::Blue, "magenta" => Color::Magenta, "cyan" => Color::Cyan, _ => Color::Red,
    };
    Style { fg: Some(c), ..Default::default() }
}
fn overlaps(spans: &[Span], s: usize, e: usize) -> bool {
    for sp in spans { if s < sp.end && e > sp.start { return true; } }
    false

        // For now, handle quotes empty as: add span with empty style, and generate_output will output text + "\x1b[0m" for empty spans? But other empty spans (like numbers empty?         }

        if sp.style.is_empty() {
            // quotes empty bug: text + reset
            out.push_str(text);
            out.push_str("\x1b[0m");
        } else {
            let open = sp.style.to_ansi_open();
            if sp.is_keyword_bg && sp.style.bg.is_some() {

            } else {
                out.push_str(&format!("{}{}\x1b[0m", open, text));
            }
        }

    }

fn highlight_kv_plain(plain: &mut String, spans: &mut Vec<Span>, theme: &Theme) {
    static RE: OnceLock<Regex> = OnceLock::new();
    let re = RE.get_or_init(|| Regex::new(r"\b(\w+)=").unwrap());
    let pc = plain.clone();
    let mut ns: Vec<Span> = Vec::new();
    for caps in re.captures_iter(&pc) {
        let m = caps.get(0).unwrap();
        let (s,e) = (m.start(), m.end());
        if overlaps(spans, s, e) || overlaps(&ns, s, e) { continue; }
        let key = caps.get(1).unwrap();
        let (ks,ke) = (key.start(), key.end());
        if !theme.kv_key.is_empty() {
            if !overlaps(spans, ks, ke) && !overlaps(&ns, ks, ke) {
                ns.push(Span{start:ks, end:ke, style: theme.kv_key.clone(), is_keyword_bg:false});

        }
        // "=" at ke..ke+1
        if !theme.kv_sep.is_empty() {
            if !overlaps(spans, ke, ke+1) && !overlaps(&ns, ke, ke+1) {
                ns.push(Span{start:ke, end:ke+1, style: theme.kv_sep.clone(), is_keyword_bg:false});
            }
        }
    }
    spans.extend(ns);
